items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: another tune that Irving Ashby, (PHONETIC) the guitar player, wrote

ctx.x: Well, it was already a big band when we made those things. In between the rehearsals, Lionel wanted to make some records and we just did that. Those fellas had just met each other, the fellas that you afore mentioned had just met each other probably a week or so before and so we made up some tunes and recorded them. I think "Bouncing at the Beacon" was mine, was my tune, and another tune called -- we named after a guy that had a radio program up in San Francisco called "Open

House," "The Open House Show." That was my tune called "Open House." Then there was another tune that Irving Ashby, (PHONETIC) the guitar player, wrote called "Stratosphere." No, it was not "Stratosphere," "Altitude," and some other things like that.

On the tune, on that particular session, the tune -- my wife, who was the vocalist in the band, Evelyn, she sang a tune called "I Nearly Lost My Mind" on one of the records, which was very, very badly recorded, wrong tempo, wrong key, wrong everything. It wasn't a good recording at all and didn't do her justice at all.
